newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian vice president urges Samper to resign.
newsitem.headline: Colombian vice president urges Samper to resign.

text.p: Colombian Vice President Humberto de la Calle urged President Ernesto Samper to resign Thursday for the good of Colombia and his fellow countrymen.

De la Calle said it was Samper's "inescapable duty" to resign because he had lost control over a nation reeling from growing poverty and violence and was seen as an illegimate head of state by half the population.
"Colombia, in short, seems to be falling to pieces," De la Calle said, referring to spiralling violence in the countryside, rising unemployment and a sharp economic slowdown so far this year.

He said the country was like a ship without a rudder and the government, weakened by charges that Samper used drug money to finance his 19894 election campaign, appeared "incapable of guaranteeing the security of civilians" amid a recent surge in leftist guerrilla activity.
De la Calle stepped down as Colombia's ambassador to Spain last month.
He issued his statement urging Samper to resign on his return from a visit to the United States where he asked earlier this week for a temporary leave of absence from his post as vice president.
